name: NGC 5668, SN 2004G field (Hubble)
blurb: NGC 5668, a spiral galaxy and host of the supernova SN 2004G, seen by Hubble.
label: sn2004ghost-hubble
story: A nearly face-on spiral galaxy that forms new stars more quickly than our Milky Way. Hubble looked around the site of SN 2004G, a Type II supernova, to learn what kinds of stars end their lives this way.

claims.text: NGC 5668 is seen nearly face-on and forms stars faster than the Milky Way
SN 2004G is a Type II supernova in NGC 5668
The Hubble program targeting SN2004G studies stellar populations around Type II supernovae
